title: The Body of the Cosmos and the Soul Bound in Its Members
description: T38 expounds the natural mind, taken as a whole, fashioned as one body answering at every part to a faculty of the rational — head as highest firmament, neck through seven firmaments, spine through five storehouses, ribs as side firmaments, navel through twelve fixed states, heart as proper human affection, thighs reaching toward the bearing principle, fire-wall of love at the outermost — with five divine watchers stationed as the five-faculty answer to the paradox of how the unchanging Lord can be bound in the smallness of the body. T39 describes how Adam was formed from the failed productions of fallen attention, and how the Lord goes down at every watch to bear up what withered. T40 traces the soul bound in the body's twelve members: mind in bone, thought in sinew, teaching in vein, counsel in flesh, reflection in skin — and the exact inverse exchange by which the Lord raises each soul-faculty out and binds the proprium's correlate in its place.
